title: Asymptotic behaviour of the derivative expansion in the ERG
abstract: We show that the derivative expansion of the exact (functional) renormalization group is a divergent series in any dimension, both for an exponential cutoff and more general smooth cutoffs. We prove this by showing that within massless $λ\varphi^4$ perturbation theory, such divergences arise first at two loops. From several lines of theoretical argument and by analysing infinite classes of two- and three-loop contributions, we conclude that the derivative expansion is an asymptotic series that initially converges towards the exact result before divergent behaviour takes over.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously demonstrates that approximating the exact renormalization group flow using a derivative expansion results in a divergent series. However, it establishes that this divergence implies the series is asymptotic, meaning accurate physical predictions can still be extracted by summing up to a specific optimal number of terms before the breakdown occurs.
main_problem: The paper investigates the convergence properties of applying the derivative expansion technique within the functional renormalization group (ERG) flow equation.
main_result: It proves that the derivative expansion is a divergent series in any dimension for both exponential and general smooth cutoffs, but it behaves as an asymptotic series.
method: The authors use perturbative calculations involving one-, two-, and three-loop contributions to analyze how derivatives ($\partial^{2n}$) appear in the effective action approximation.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed using massless lambda phi^4 theory, a standard model in quantum and statistical field theory studied via FRG techniques.
key_observables: Convergence behavior of the derivative expansion series; $ eta$-functions and self-energies ($\Gamma(p, -p)$).
important_parameters: Spacetime dimension (d); loop order ($\ell$); number of derivatives ($2n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of an additive IR cutoff function for the FRG flow equation.
paper_structure: The paper develops arguments by analyzing loop contributions and comparing convergence rates across different vertex types (2-point, 4-point, etc.) to establish the asymptotic nature of the expansion.
why_interesting: While focused on QFT methods, understanding the limitations and convergence radii of systematic approximations like derivative expansions is crucial for developing reliable non-perturbative tools applicable in complex many-body systems studied by AMO physicists.
